CHARACTER HEADER NATIVE SOURCE DECOMPILATION
Static disk-only extraction from the configured native Windows PE images.
Steam renderer unwind range: 0x14014ef90..0x1401a01c4
Classic renderer unwind range: 0x14014ef20..0x1401a0154
The screenshots correspond to the selected-unit title block; all references below are within its code paths, not a whole-image string grep.

CONTROL FLOW (Steam VA):
0x14015aa0e: if viewscreen+0x1900, render the nickname and custom-profession editing fields. The two dynamic fields use unit.name+0x20 and unit+0x80. The only fixed text here is '_' (blinking caret). Existing icons are drawn as tile IDs, not English labels.
0x14015b8be: default header obtains full name/profession at 0x141330c30. If too wide, obtain name at 0x141330500 and profession at 0x141330880, print on two lines, clip with literal '.' bytes. User nickname/custom profession and RAW names are dynamic source values.
0x14015bbf0: arena/game-mode 4 replaces translated-name second row with Independent (unit+0x1270 == 0), else '#' + numeric team id.
0x14015becf..0x14015c20f: resolve currently visible historical identity / apparent identity, obtain English translated generated name at 0x140a946e0, and draw double quotes around it (character 0x22).
0x14015c20f: establish next header row. Below is a priority chain; only the first eligible state/description is emitted.
1. soldier_mood (unit+0x814) != -1: 0=In a martial trance!; 1=Enraged at all enemies!; 2=Throwing a tantrum!; 3=Sunk into depression...; 4=Stumbling obliviously!; other=Corrupt Soldier Mood: + decimal enum.
2. strange_mood (unit+0x360) not in [-1,8]: 0=Has the aspect of one fey!; 1=Peculiarly secretive...; 2=Possessed by unknown forces!; 3=Brooding darkly...; 4=Has a horrible fell look!; 5=Stricken by melancholy...; 6=Running/Crawling around babbling! or crazed!, selected by sapience/intelligence query and unit+0x110 &0x8000; 7=In a berserk rage!; 9=Staring off into space...; other=Corrupt Strange Mood: + decimal enum.
3. unit+0x118 &0x2000000: walk unit soul (unit+0xa98), emotion vector soul+0x278, until the first recognized emotion whose +0x18 flags &1. The enum switch is compressed through tables at 0x14019eaec and 0x14019eaa8. Codes: 5 Writhing in agony!; 12 In existential crisis!; 13 Anguished!; 39 Lost in despair!; 44 Completely dismayed!; 46 Distressed!; 64 Experiencing mortal fear!; 68 Taken by a fright!; 78 Beside {herself|himself|itself} with grief!; 88 Overwhelmed by horror!; 111 Wallowing in misery!; 112 Truly mortified!; 135 Drowning in sadness!; 141 Shaken to the core!; 143 In emotional shock!; 152 Overcome by terror!. Otherwise Emotionally overloaded!.
4. unit owner id (unit+0x3bc) != -1 and owner eligibility 0x14138ed20: draw 'Pet of ' first; get owner by 0x14134f250; if present generate owner name(owner+8) via 0x140a94030, otherwise 'Somebody'; draw owner separately at same current row and x advanced by the prefix. No reposition call occurs between prefix and name.
5. unit+0x11c &0x800: draw 'Creator of ' first; initialize empty string, generate unit+0xa08 language_name via 0x140a94030; draw resulting name separately on same current row. No reposition call between prefix and name, and no empty-name fallback.
6. no historical figure or histfig+0xac == -1: office/position resolver 0x1413cbbd0, entity_position gendered/plural/spouse label getter 0x14099a3c0 (names +0x98/+0xd8/+0x118 etc.), uppercase first char 0x14052d3c0; append territorial qualification via 0x1409bdfb0 when position+0x2c8 >0. Sources are entity POSITION NAME / NAME_MALE / NAME_FEMALE / spouse forms and linked site/entity names. This is an office label, not a creature/caste name.
0x14015d588..0x14015d6f8: next activity/job line; query unit flag 0x3a, resolve job unit+0x4d8, if job flag+0x2c &0x10000 is clear get label at 0x140d03170, otherwise fallback activity 0x141390cf0.
0x14015d706: header exit; following code draws expel UI/modal, outside this title block.

GENERATED NAME (foreign name 0x140a94030..0x140a946d1):
Input language_name+0x72 is the has_name byte. If 0 it returns without appending any output. Creator branch only checks artifact-creator flag and does not check this byte or a generated-name result before drawing its prefix; empty artifact text is therefore permitted in native game code and appears already empty in the English screenshot. Actual save fields are unavailable here, so this explains native possibility rather than diagnosing the exact save field.
When named: first-name string at +0x0, nickname string at +0x20, word IDs at +0x40..+0x58, grammatical parts at +0x5c..+0x68, language id +0x6c. Their spellings come from runtime RAW LANGUAGE/TRANSLATION tables. Fixed punctuation is spaces, backtick/apostrophe.
Translated-name generator 0x140a946e0..0x140a94ea2 reads the same IDs and grammatical parts through 0x140d2cb50; fixed grammatical particles are The / the / Of / of. Generated proper names are compositional and not a finite list of full sentences; custom names accept arbitrary author text.

GENERATED-NAME LEXICAL SOURCE CHAIN
Native disassembly: foreign-name 0x140a94030 reads game translation vectors at 0x1424ed770/0x1424ed7a0, language_name word IDs +0x40..+0x58 and language ID +0x6c. English-name 0x140a946e0 calls 0x140d2cb50 for the grammatical English surface of each WORD slot, then assembles optional The/the/Of/of articles and word groups. These are RAW LANGUAGE [WORD] and [TRANSLATION]/[T_WORD] sources, not a finite list of full displayed proper names. The author-entered first-name/nickname/custom-profession string fields are arbitrary text.
Static source files in BOTH configured installations: data/vanilla/vanilla_languages/objects/language_words.txt, language_DWARF.txt, language_ELF.txt, language_GOBLIN.txt, language_HUMAN.txt; language_SYM.txt groups existing WORD identities through SYMBOL/S_WORD and contributes no new spelling.
Each installed language_words source contains 2196 WORD identities, 3301 WORD/POS definitions (NOUN/ADJ/VERB/PREFIX), and 5919 distinct English word forms, including inflections. Every identity/POS pair is present in dfcn/data/runtime/procedural-word-senses.tsv; every form is present in procedural-terms.tsv. Thus no finite English lexical omission was found in the name getters' RAW source vocabulary.
Each native TRANSLATION source contains 2196 T_WORD records. The four translation tables collectively expose 8433 distinct CP437 spellings, all linked to available WORD identities. DFCN recognizes the four exact files in Overlay::load_generated_instrument_names, src/dfcn.cpp:6094..6158; retains language masks and WORD IDs; imports reviewed pronunciations from existing title-case wi rules and scoped 'Native name pronunciation: ' h rules at src/dfcn.cpp:6161..6187. Remaining native words use existing transliterate_native_history_name, src/history_names.inc:3; accented CP437 capitals fold in src/dfcn.cpp:176. Lack of a handwritten phonetic dictionary entry does not imply an untranslated name: this existing fallback renders the native spelling phonetically.
English senses load in src/dfcn.cpp:6201 and grammar forms/WORD+POS roles in src/dfcn.cpp:6268..6475; procedural forms load in src/dfcn.cpp:6479. Foreign two-root surname decoding keeps WORD identity, language, and compound roles at src/dfcn.cpp:9249..9295. Native title groups allow up to four roots and an OfX root at src/dfcn.cpp:9312..9348; named-item grammar uses these at src/dfcn.cpp:9350..9393. Native-history-name slots resolve Chinese semantic WORD/POS senses in src/history_names.inc:228 onward. Reviewed source namespaces are procedural-terms (English surface forms), procedural-word-senses (WORD/POS semantics), title-case wi/scoped pronunciation h entries (native phonetics), and native_name lexical language masks (the RAW T_WORD roots).
No local installed mod adds [WORD], [TRANSLATION], or [T_WORD]: both data/installed_mods directories contain no text objects; Steam mods contains three txt files without LANGUAGE vocabulary objects; classic has no mods directory. This is bounded to the two configured game installations, not assumptions about downloaded worlds or unknown future mods. New mod-defined WORD identities would require explicit WORD/POS senses and native-language-root loading; arbitrary authored names cannot be enumerated as finite English sentences.
This source comparison does not constitute observation of an in-game rendered result.

ACTIVITY / CURRENT JOB CALL GRAPH
The final header row uses the two actual native entry paths below. These are the Windows PE paths; the older ELF formatter offsets and slots are not substituted.
Steam: header job call 0x14015d697 -> 0x140d03170 -> 0x140d032b0; activity entry 0x141390cf0 -> 0x14138ffd0..0x141390c7c.
Classic: header job call 0x14015d627 -> 0x140d001b0 -> 0x140d002f0; activity call 0x14015d659 -> 0x14138bc60 -> 0x14138af40.
Each activity formatter selects the current job, the activity_event virtual method at vtable+0xb0, a squad_order virtual method at vtable+0x68, direct meeting/resident/idle state, or a diplomatic action followed by its typed site name. The complete MSVC chained unwind ranges are used; leaf skill/topic/sphere switch ranges do not have ordinary unwind entries.
Actual methods and references for both editions are retained in character-header-activity-bindings.tsv and character-header-activity-sources.tsv. Their source categories are status, job, activity, order, skill, topic, sphere, article, RAW reaction NAME, and generated instrument NAME prefix.
CustomReaction jobs use the selected reaction RAW NAME and capitalize its first letter (Steam 0x140d0743d..0x140d07485). The currently installed reaction sources are retained by file and line in the same source table. Object-bearing jobs/events retain their typed item/material/instrument/person/site data; strings such as 'Go to ', ' at ', or '/Resting' are grammatical fragments rather than independent complete tasks.
The existing strict header activity recognizer accepts Fortress activity exact captions before a blank separator. A generic global translation alone does not prove activity identity there. Complete fixed captions and the RAW wooden-helve reaction therefore receive this scope in local-overrides.tsv; dynamic object grammar remains shared with the item/name/material/activity resolvers.
